title: Vertex AI Automation: Set Up a Scheduled Pipeline in 2026
summary: Vertex AI automation runs your models unattended on a schedule in Google Cloud. You'll set up pipelines that trigger automatically or from workflow events.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions and when Activepieces fits


If something outside Google Cloud must start the job or receive its result, Activepieces fits, with 750 integrations in its open source monorepo to cover the form, CRM or webhook. Vertex AI's own tools fit everything else.


In Activepieces, an automation platform, a trigger starts a chain of steps, and one step can call the Vertex AI API over HTTP. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


It doesn't replace Vertex AI. It carries the request in and the answer out, so the Google-side permissions, quotas and region still apply.


As a rule of thumb, Activepieces fits when a job must start from a form, CRM or webhook, and results go to Slack or email. The free plan includes unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, so a first job of that shape costs $0.


Native tools stay right for training and large pipelines.


### Can Vertex AI run workflows without code?


Partly. The Google Cloud console lets you create a schedule or launch a batch prediction without writing a program, but a pipeline definition is code.


If the missing integration is a trigger or a notification, Activepieces covers it without code, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has. The service account behind it still needs the right permissions, and someone still has to own it.


Does Vertex AI automation cost extra beyond model usage? Usually yes, though the lines differ. Pipeline runs consume compute and storage, scheduled jobs and logging can add their own charges, and an outside automation platform may bill or host separately.


Check each pricing page before the first run. Skip this and the result is a monthly invoice no one can attribute to a job.


How is Vertex AI Pipelines different from Cloud Scheduler? Start with timing: Cloud Scheduler decides when something fires. Vertex AI Pipelines decides what runs, in what order, with what inputs and outputs between steps.


A scheduler can start a pipeline, but it knows nothing about whether step three succeeded. For the smallest first job, a schedule calling one endpoint is enough. Reach for Pipelines when steps depend on each other.


### Can I call Gemini on Vertex AI from an outside app?


Yes. Any app that can send an authenticated HTTPS request can call a Gemini model through the Vertex AI endpoint.


It needs credentials for a service account allowed to use the model, and the request must name a region where that model is available.


A region mismatch is one of the failures this article keeps returning to, so test with one request before wiring in the trigger. Then record who owns that service account in the runbook.
